newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan reactor leaks radioactive acid solution.
newsitem.headline: Japan reactor leaks radioactive acid solution.

text.p: Shikoku Electric Power Co Inc said that slightly radioactive boric acid solution leaked out of a waste tank of one of the nuclear reactors at its Ikata power plant in western Japan on Thursday morning.
"About five cubic metres of boric acid solution overflowed from a waste tank onto the floor of the building housing the storage tank," a company spokesman said.
"But according to our monitor devices, there seems to be no impact on the environment," he added.
The utility originally planned to put the boric acid solution into the waste tank storing low-level radioactive water after removing some water from the tank to make room.
But the solution was sent to the waste tank before this as a valve on a pipe connecting the tank containing the boric acid solution with the waste tank was left open, he said.
The 890,000-kilowatt (kw) reactor on Shikoku, the smallest of Japan four major islands, has been closed since May 16 for routine maintenance, which was originally scheduled to last about two months.
The official said it was not yet clear whether the accident would delay the restarting of the reactor.
He said the two other reactors at the plant, each of which has a power generation capacity of 566,000 kw, were running normally.
